source: transcribed from the run on the Linux host of the author, see bench/native_comparison.sh
notes: Both programs run natively on the same host, with the same weights, and produce the same tokens, so the comparison is of the arithmetic and not of the model.
The reference is PyTorch in eager mode and float32. Its dispatcher and autograd are part of what it costs, and a compiled or quantized build would be a different comparison.
The number of tokens per second varies by around thirty per cent between runs on this host, so the figures are a sample and not a precise measurement.
The runtime pins the weights, and the pin costs about seventy milliseconds of the time to the first token.
The llama.cpp measurement is missing because the conversion of the checkpoint was not available; it is optional because a converted checkpoint is a different precision.
